title: L&T Subsidiary Bags Mega Order to Build India's Largest NVIDIA B300 AI Factory
excerpt: LTN Compute partners with Together AI to deploy 10,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs at L&T's Chennai campus, marking the infrastructure giant's formal entry into the AI factory business.
body:
• L&T's subsidiary LTN Compute has secured a mega order to build India's largest NVIDIA B300 AI Factory in partnership with US-based Together AI
  • The facility will deploy 10,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs at L&T's 300-acre Chennai campus, which is being scaled to 30 MW capacity
  • The order marks L&T's formal entry into the AI Factory business, building on its February 2026 partnership with NVIDIA
  • L&T is also building a separate 40 MW data center in Mumbai as part of its broader gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure push

LTN Compute Enters AI Factory Business

Larsen & Toubro's subsidiary LTN Compute has secured a mega order to build India's largest NVIDIA B300 AI Factory, the company disclosed in a regulatory filing to the BSE on August 13. The order, placed in partnership with US-based AI infrastructure company Together AI, will see 10,000 NVIDIA B300 GPUs deployed at a facility in India.

The deal establishes L&T's presence in the rapidly growing AI factory business, a segment that has attracted massive global investment as companies race to build dedicated computing infrastructure for training and deploying AI models. NVIDIA's B300 GPU is its latest Blackwell-generation chip, designed for large-scale AI workloads.

"India's enterprises are ready to move from AI pilots to production-scale deployment. The investment establishes the foundation — secure, scalable, and sovereign infrastructure — required to power manufacturing, energy, financial services, healthcare, and public services."

— S.N. Subrahmanyan, Chairman & Managing Director, L&T

Building on the NVIDIA Partnership

The mega order is the first major commercial outcome of L&T's strategic partnership with NVIDIA, announced in February 2026 at the India AI Summit in Mumbai. That partnership, struck under India's IndiaAI Mission, outlined plans for L&T to combine its engineering and infrastructure capabilities with NVIDIA's AI hardware and software stack to build gigawatt-scale AI data center infrastructure.

Under the plan, L&T is scaling NVIDIA GPU cluster deployments at its Chennai data center to 30 MW capacity within a 300-acre campus designed for gigawatt-scale expansion. The company is also building a new 40 MW data center in Mumbai.

Together AI, L&T's partner on this order, is a San Francisco-based company that provides cloud infrastructure for running and fine-tuning AI models. The company has emerged as a significant player in the AI infrastructure market, offering developers access to high-performance GPU clusters.

India's AI Infrastructure Push

The order comes amid a broader push by India to build out sovereign AI computing capacity. The Indian government has approved over ₹10,300 crore ($1.24 billion) in funding for its IndiaAI Mission, which includes plans for a public-private partnership to build AI computing infrastructure with at least 10,000 GPUs.

L&T's AI factory is designed as sovereign infrastructure, meaning AI workloads, data, and models can be built and deployed within India while remaining compatible with global systems. The facility will serve domestic enterprises as well as global hyperscalers and cloud providers seeking AI capacity based in India.

"AI is driving the largest infrastructure buildout in human history — everyone will use it, every company will be powered by it, and every country will build it."

— Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO, NVIDIA

Strategic Shift for L&T

For L&T, the move represents a strategic pivot toward high-growth digital infrastructure. The $30 billion conglomerate, traditionally known for engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) projects, has been diversifying into technology and data center services. Earlier this month, L&T divested its data center and cloud services business to its wholly-owned subsidiary Vyoma.AI Limited for ₹1,400 crore, signaling a restructuring of its digital infrastructure assets.

The company's broader order book remains robust. In recent weeks, L&T has secured an ultra-mega order worth over ₹15,000 crore from ADNOC Offshore and a batch of major offshore orders from ONGC valued between ₹5,000 crore and ₹10,000 crore. But the AI factory order represents a fundamentally different kind of business — one tied to the global AI infrastructure buildout rather than traditional construction.

Target sectors for the AI factory include manufacturing, energy, financial services, healthcare, and public services. L&T's own group companies, including LTTS and LTM, plan to deploy AI agents on the sovereign cloud infrastructure.
